name: python-guide
Python guardrails for Python files, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, or Python requests. Applies to Python 3.11+ APIs, CLIs, data pipelines, automation.

## Standards
- All function signatures, class attributes, and module-level variables must have type annotations. All public functions MUST have full type annotations (params + return).
- No `*` imports, no mutable default arguments, no implicit type coercions. Never use bare `except:` or `except Exception:` without re-raising.
- Never install into system Python; use `venv`, `uv`, or `poetry`.
- Use pytest for all testing; fixtures and parametrize over setUp/tearDown. No `unittest.TestCase` — use plain functions with pytest assertions.
- Enforce PEP 8 + Ruff mechanically; never rely on manual formatting. Run `ruff check` and `ruff format` before every commit.
- Target Python 3.11+: use `match`, `ExceptionGroup`, `tomllib`; set `requires-python = ">=3.11"` in `pyproject.toml`. Use `from __future__ import annotations` for forward references in 3.11. Never use features removed in 3.12+ (`distutils`, `imp`, legacy `typing` aliases).
- Max line length 88. Import order: stdlib, third-party, local (blank lines between); enforced by `isort`/`ruff`.
- Naming: `snake_case`, `PascalCase`, `UPPER_SNAKE`.
- Prefer f-strings; use `pathlib.Path` instead of `os.path` for all file operations.
- Use `collections.abc` types (`Sequence`, `Mapping`, `Iterable`), not `List`/`Dict`; use `X | None`, not `Optional[X]`. Use `TypeAlias` for complex types and `Protocol` for structural subtyping. Use `<REDACTED_USER>` for functions returning different types based on input.
- Run `mypy --strict` in CI (no `type: ignore` without explanation).
- Create domain-specific exception hierarchies rooted in a base class. Use `raise ... from err`; log at the boundary, raise in the interior (don't log-and-raise). Use `contextlib.suppress()` instead of empty except blocks. Always close resources with `with` statements or `contextlib.closing`.
- Define all deps in `pyproject.toml` (not `setup.py` or bare `requirements.txt`). Pin exact versions in lock files (`uv.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `pip-compile` output). Keep `requirements.txt` only as a generated artifact, never hand-edited. Separate `[project.optional-dependencies]` for dev, test, docs. Audit with `pip-audit` or `safety` before adding new packages. Prefer stdlib solutions: `tomllib`, `pathlib`, `dataclasses`, `enum`, `logging`.

## Project/testing
Use `src/myproject/` src layout; include `py.typed`. Keep `conftest.py` at test root for shared fixtures; nest for scope. No `__init__.py` in `tests/`. One module = one responsibility; split at ~200 lines.
Test files `test_*.py` (e.g. `models.py` -> `test_models.py`); functions `test_<unit>_<scenario>_<expected>`. Coverage: >80% business logic, >60% overall. Mark slow tests: `<REDACTED_USER>.mark.slow` and exclude from default runs. Use `tmp_path` for file operations.

## Configuration examples
```toml
[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["ruff", "mypy", "pytest", "pytest-cov", "pytest-asyncio"]
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"
[tool.ruff.lint]
# "S" (flake8-bandit), "SIM" (flake8-simplify), "RUF" (ruff-specific rules)
warn_return_any = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
markers = ["slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/myproject"]
[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
exclude_lines = ["if TYPE_CHECKING:", "pragma: no cover"]
```

## Commands
```sh
ruff check .                 # Lint (replaces flake8, isort, pyupgrade)
ruff format .                # Format (replaces black)
mypy .                       # Type check (strict mode)
pytest                       # Run all tests
pytest --cov=src -q          # Coverage summary
pytest -m "not slow"         # Skip slow tests
pip-audit                    # Check dependencies for vulnerabilities
python -m build              # Build sdist + wheel
```

Examples/patterns: [references/patterns.md](references/patterns.md) (async, models, context managers, decorators, typing); [references/pitfalls.md](references/pitfalls.md); [references/security.md](references/security.md). See PEP 8, PEP 484, Ruff, mypy, pytest, Python Packaging Guide, Effective Python.
